The text uses outdated and potentially offensive terminology by referring to "the blind." Inclusive language best practices recommend using person-first or identity-first language that respects individuality, such as "people who are blind" or "blind individuals." Referring to a group as "the blind" can be seen as dehumanizing or overly reductive.

Regarding accessibility features, the text mentions tactile floor plans and audio descriptions, which are positive accommodations for visually impaired individuals. However, the audit should also consider whether other sensory or cognitive needs are addressed, though the text focuses solely on visual impairment.

The color of a common crow is black.
